chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man urinated and did not have water with him. He said: "He should squeeze the root of his penis to the tip of his penis three squeezes, and shake its tip. Then if something comes out after that, it is not from urine, but rather it is from the passages."

key_terms.الْحَبَائِلِ: the passages/veins from which non-urinary residual moisture may emerge
key_terms.يَعْصِرُ: he squeezes, as part of cleansing after urination

ai.seo_question: What should a person do after urinating without water to ensure later discharge is not considered urine?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity after urination when water is not available. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام instructs a method of istibrāʾ so that any discharge emerging afterward is not treated as urine, which has significance for taharah and acts of worship.
